new_quiz.q: What is a test stage for animation?
choices: A large level with finished art
A small, simple level with objects of known sizes
A window that lists all animations
A camera that records the viewport
new_quiz.explain: A test stage is a small level with things such as a step, a ledge and a gap of known sizes. It is a fixed place to judge motion.

new_quiz.q: Why do the objects on the stage have known sizes with labels?
choices: So the level loads faster
So the lights can be placed by size
So the mannequin gets collision
So you can check that a character moves at the right scale
new_quiz.explain: A step of about 20 cm or a gap of about 2 m is a ruler for the character. Next to them you see at once if the mesh or the motion has the wrong scale.

new_quiz.q: How do you make a Skeletal Mesh Actor play one run or walk sequence?
choices: Set Animation Mode to Use Animation Asset and choose the sequence
Set Mobility to Static and press Play
Add a Timeline to the Level Blueprint
Drag the sequence onto the Directional Light
new_quiz.explain: With Animation Mode set to Use Animation Asset, the actor plays the single animation you choose. No Animation Blueprint is needed.

new_quiz.q: The mannequin plays its run one time and then stands still. What did you forget?
choices: To add a Sky Light
To set Anim Class to ABP_Unarmed
To enable Looping
To place a Camera Actor
new_quiz.explain: Without Looping the animation asset plays once and stops. With Looping enabled it starts again each time it ends.

new_quiz.q: Why do you place a second mannequin with its Anim Class set to ABP_Unarmed?
choices: So the stage has two Player Starts
So you can compare an animation asset with an Animation Blueprint
So the first mannequin runs faster
So the clip is twice as long
new_quiz.explain: One mannequin plays a single looping asset, and the other is driven by the Animation Blueprint of the template. Side by side, the difference is easy to see.

new_quiz.q: What is the extra light on the stage for?
choices: It makes the mannequin easy to see from the front
It replaces the Directional Light
It shows the size of the gap
It lights the stage from below
new_quiz.explain: The Directional Light and the Sky Light give the base lighting. The extra light makes sure the front of the mannequin is clear, so the motion is easy to read.

new_quiz.q: What is a shot board?
choices: A list of the cameras in a level
A panel where you edit a sequence
One page of still images in order that tell a small story
A light setup with three lamps
new_quiz.explain: A shot board puts a few stills on one page in order. It shows that you can frame, light and focus a shot before anything is animated.

new_quiz.q: Which three shots do you plan for the board?
choices: A wide establishing shot, a medium shot and a close-up
A top shot, a side shot and a front shot
A day shot, a night shot and a fog shot
A fast shot, a slow shot and a still shot
new_quiz.explain: The three shots go from far to near. Together they lead the viewer from the whole place to one detail.

new_quiz.q: What does the wide establishing shot show?
choices: Only the face of the subject
Only the key light
The cameras and the lights
The whole place
new_quiz.explain: An establishing shot tells the viewer where they are. It shows the whole place before the closer shots pick out parts of it.

new_quiz.q: What is the key light in your lighting pass?
choices: The light that fills the shadows
The main light
The light from the sky
The light behind the camera
new_quiz.explain: The key light is the main light of the shot. A fill light or a sky light then softens the shadows it makes.

new_quiz.q: How do you check the framing of each camera?
choices: Switch the view mode to Shader Complexity
Run stat unit in the console
Turn on the Cinematic Viewport and use the Grid (3x3) overlay
Open the Output Log and filter for cameras
new_quiz.explain: The Cinematic Viewport shows the picture the way the camera frames it. The Grid (3x3) overlay draws guide lines that help you place the subject.

new_quiz.q: What does each still on the board show next to it?
choices: Its file size and date
Its one-line description, focal length and aperture
Its light count and frame rate
Its level name and folder
new_quiz.explain: The line says what the viewer should notice. The focal length and the aperture record how the camera was set for that shot.

new_quiz.q: What is a toy space?
choices: A level full of finished art and no gameplay
A folder for unused Blueprints
A menu where the player picks a level
The smallest thing that is still a game
new_quiz.explain: A toy space has one action for the player, one room, and one number on screen. It is small enough to finish and still a real game.

new_quiz.q: What is a player verb?
choices: One action the player does, such as jump or collect
The name of the player character
A text shown on the screen
A variable that stores the score
new_quiz.explain: A verb is an action such as jump, dash, collect or push. You pick one, and every space in the room must use it.

new_quiz.q: What does it mean to graybox a room?
choices: To light it with gray lights only
To hide it from the player
To build it with basic shapes only and no art
To copy it from another project
new_quiz.explain: A graybox uses simple shapes. You can test and change the room quickly, because no art has to be redone.

new_quiz.q: How do you make the Float variable of your BP_Toy_ actor Instance Editable?
choices: Rename it so that it starts with BP_
Click the eye icon next to the variable
Set its Category to Tuning
Add a Tooltip to it
new_quiz.explain: The eye icon next to a variable turns on Instance Editable. The value can then be tuned on each placed copy in the Details panel.

new_quiz.q: Which of these is a flow control node?
choices: Branch
Print String
Add to Viewport
Get Actor Location
new_quiz.explain: Flow control nodes decide which path the execution takes. Branch, Gate, DoOnce and FlipFlop are flow control nodes.

new_quiz.q: Where do you tune the speed or the jump of the character for your room?
choices: In the World Settings of the level
In the Widget Blueprint of the score
In the Play options of the main toolbar
On the Character Movement component of BP_ThirdPersonCharacter
new_quiz.explain: The Character Movement component holds the movement values of the character. Changing them there fits the character to the size of your room.

new_quiz.q: What is a test bed for a technical artist?
choices: A small level built only for testing
A tool that renames assets by a rule
A list of all the stat commands
A material with many parameters
new_quiz.explain: A test bed is one known place where you check things under the same light every time. That makes problems easy to spot.

new_quiz.q: In the Construction Script of BP_FenceRow, why do you call Clear Instances before the loop?
choices: So the mesh gets a new material
So the loop starts at index 1
So old instances do not pile up each time the script runs again
So the actor is deleted from the level
new_quiz.explain: The Construction Script runs again when you change a setting of the actor in the editor. Clearing first removes the old instances before the loop adds the new ones.

new_quiz.q: In the loop, X is set to the loop index times Spacing. What does this do?
choices: It makes each instance larger than the last
It places each instance one Spacing further along a row
It rotates each instance around the first
It gives each instance a random position
new_quiz.explain: Index 0 gives X 0, index 1 gives one Spacing, index 2 gives two, and so on. The instances form an even row.

new_quiz.q: How do you make the Niagara system for the room?
choices: Open Landscape Mode and choose New
Add a Timeline to the Level Blueprint
Enable the Water plugin and restart
In the Content Browser, choose FX, then Niagara System
new_quiz.explain: Niagara System is in the FX group of the Content Browser menu. The Fountain template gives you a working effect, and its name should start with FXS_.

new_quiz.q: What does the Shader Complexity view mode show?
choices: How many lights touch each mesh
How many triangles each mesh has
How costly the materials are to draw on each pixel
How much memory each texture uses
new_quiz.explain: Shader Complexity colors the picture by the cost of the materials on each pixel. Cheap areas are green and costly areas go toward red and white.

new_quiz.q: Which prefixes do the assets in the TechArt folder get?
choices: BP_ for Blueprints, FXS_ for Niagara systems, M_ for materials and L_ for levels
A_ for all assets, in the order they were made
TA_ for every asset in the folder
No prefixes, because the folder name is enough
new_quiz.explain: A prefix tells the kind of asset from the name alone. With correct prefixes, anyone can search and sort the folder.
